title: A 5-degree time shuffle showed excess depth similarity in shallow ComCat pairs in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested depth similarity in 10,464 ComCat earthquakes with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth from 0 to below 70 km in 2000-2025. There were 5,470 same-year pairs within 100 km and 1-7 days. We removed the mean depth gap in each 10 km surface-distance bin of the same-year candidate pool. The observed adjusted mean was -1.166 km. In 9,999 time shuffles within year and 5-degree cells, the mean was -0.558 km and the lower-tail p-value was 0.0052. A post hoc 1-degree shuffle reduced the difference to 0.370 km, with p = 0.0259. A 2013-2025 check was inconclusive (p = 0.1463), as was removal of integer depths (p = 0.1356). The primary result shows an association under the stated time-exchangeability assumption. It does not establish a fault plane, triggering mechanism, or freedom from catalog error. Fine geography, fixed depths, shared events, location errors, mixed magnitude scales and revised data limit use. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a numerical audit and a figure are included. Raw records and derived pair tables remain external.
